data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The published distinction (per RFC 9110 \u00a79.2.1) is sharper than the informal one: 'safe' means the operation has no side effects at all\u2014it is semantically read-only, intended to be callable without any risk of changing observable state. 'Idempotent' means repeated identical invocations have the same effect as a single one, but side effects are permitted. An append-only event log's writers are neither safe nor idempotent in this strict sense. What the log actually requires is a weaker, informal 'retry-safe' property that neither RFC term captures: retried writes may produce duplicate entries, but those duplicates are tolerated by the replay protocol.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the problem uses 'safe' in the retry-safety sense rather than the RFC 9110 read-only sense, this framing collapses and the log does require safe (retry-safe) writers","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the replay protocol has no deduplication mechanism, the distinction is academic\u2014at-least-once delivery would produce incorrect replay regardless of terminology","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If one argues that 'no harmful side effects from retry' is itself a form of safety (broadening the RFC definition), then the log does require safe writers under the broader reading","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In RFC 9110 terminology, safe = read-only (GET), idempotent = convergent (PUT, DELETE). An append is POST-like: it has side effects (new entry) and is not convergent (two appends \u2260 one). So strictly, the log's writers are neither safe nor idempotent. The log survives at-least-once because it imposes a third property\u2014call it 'retry-tolerant'\u2014where the replay protocol is explicitly designed to handle duplicates. This property is neither safety (side effects exist) nor idempotency (state diverges), but a protocol-level guarantee that duplicates are benign.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
